event: 2025 ILCA 6 Women's & ILCA 7 Men's World Championships
procedural_matters: TPE 214123 was represented by Tsai-Chien Wu.
The organizing authority was represented by Ferdinand Ziegelmayer (representative of the boat provider).
Kamolwan Chanyim (coach of TPE 214123) attended the hearing as an observer.
Qu Chun, Jiang Zuoru, Xu Xiaolong, Zhou Dongning (all members of the international jury) and Fengyi Hu (jury secretary) attended the hearing as observers.
facts: 30 seconds before the start of race 3 for the ILCA 7 Men's Red fleet, the front deck cunningham holding ring on the right side popped out.
On 17 May 2025, TPE 214123 finished in races 3 and 4 but did not race in race 5.
TPE 214123 received his boat on 7 May 2025 for the pre-event charter period.
TPE 214123 went on the water for pre-event training and the previous five racing days.
The boat provider experienced this issue for the first time.
TPE 214123 did not report any issues regarding the boat to the organizing authority before the event started.

Notice of Race 6.9 states: "Failure of equipment supplied by the organizing authority shall not be grounds for redress, unless the international jury decides that it was the result of a manufacturing defect that could have been reasonably anticipated by the organizing authority. This changes RRS 61.4(b)(1)."
conclusions: Due to the rarity of the defect, it was not reasonably possible for the organizing authority to anticipate it.
Because it was not reasonably possible for the organizing authority to anticipate this equipment failure, it is not grounds for redress under Notice of Race 6.9.
There was neither an improper action nor improper omission of the organizing authority. Therefore, the requirements for redress in RRS 61.4(b)(1) are not met.
